defects.title: Most of the catalogue carries no Product markup
defects.detail: In the audited set — the 229 product pages that rank — 156 have only a breadcrumb. The catalogue is far larger than that: 6,549 product detail pages across 519 manufacturers. A random sample of 155 of the pages outside the audited set was checked live and 19% carried Product markup (95% confidence 13–26%). On that basis roughly 4,874–5,688 product pages have no Product markup. The 73 pages that do are excellent — SKU, brand, price, availability, condition, dimensions and a leaseLength that correctly models a rental.
defects.fix: Roll the existing product template across the catalogue, highest-traffic first. The markup pattern is already correct and already in production.

defects.title: There is no sitewide identity block
defects.detail: Organization markup appears on only 171 of 487 pages. 316 pages — including every product page and most brand pages — say nothing about who publishes them. The homepage does carry a strong LocalBusiness node with geo coordinates and opening hours, but nothing else on the site references it.
defects.fix: Emit the Organization node sitewide with a stable @id, and reference it from every Product, Article and WebPage as publisher or seller.

defects.title: Part of the catalogue no longer resolves
defects.detail: 14 of 169 sampled catalogue URLs (8%) did not return 200 — a mix of 404s and timeouts. Extrapolated across 6,549 product pages that is a meaningful number of dead product URLs still linked from elsewhere on the web and from search results.
defects.fix: Crawl the full catalogue for status codes and redirect discontinued instruments to their category or successor model rather than leaving them to 404.

defects.title: Manufacturer pages name a brand but never identify it
defects.detail: 74 manufacturer pages carry a Brand node with a name string and nothing else — no sameAs, no Organization, no link to the manufacturer's own identity. These are real companies, most of them with their own Wikidata and Wikipedia entries, and the markup treats them as free text.
defects.fix: Type each manufacturer as an Organization with sameAs pointing at its Wikidata item and official site, and reference it from every product of that brand.

defects.title: Category pages mostly lack ItemList
defects.detail: Only 12 of 72 category pages carry ItemList markup, though they are all the same kind of page: a filtered list of instruments. The twelve that do have it show the pattern works.
defects.fix: Extend the existing ItemList pattern to the remaining category pages, listing the product URLs in display order.

defects.title: Standards pages do not say which standard they are about
defects.detail: 56 compliance-standards pages cover named, published standards — MIL-STD-810, RTCA DO-160 and others — and are typed as generic WebPage or Article. Nothing states that the page is about a specific technical standard, and nothing links the standard to the equipment that tests against it.
defects.fix: Add a TechArticle or DefinedTerm node naming the standard, with sameAs to its Wikidata item, and link it to the relevant product categories.

defects.title: The services page has no structured data at all
defects.detail: 4 pages carry no JSON-LD, and /services is one of them. Calibration, repair and rental are the three things this business sells, and none of them is described as a Service.
defects.fix: Type the services page with a Service node per offering, each with provider, areaServed and serviceType.

defects.title: Application pages are typed as generic Articles
defects.detail: 23 solutions pages and 20 inspection pages explain test methods — EMC testing, ESD testing, OTDR testing, fibre splicing. They are typed as Article or WebPage. The fibre-splicing page alone is the single highest-traffic page on the site at an estimated 18,335 visits a month.
defects.fix: Type these as TechArticle with about pointing at the method's entity, and link to the instruments used and the standards involved.

defects.title: FAQ markup no longer earns a rich result
defects.detail: 2 pages carry FAQPage. Google removed the FAQ rich result from Search on 7 May 2026. The markup is still worth keeping for entity clarity and AI citation, but it should not be counted as a SERP feature.
defects.fix: Keep the markup, reset the expectation.
